---
title: "Assignments & Assessment"
subtitle: "What you'll do and how you'll be evaluated"
toc: false
---

This course is structured around five complementary forms of assessment. Quizzes and the final exam check your mastery of the textbook material. In-class writing prompts ensure you stay engaged with each day's reading. The article presentation gives you a chance to lead discussion on contemporary scholarship. And participation rewards consistent, prepared engagement throughout the four-week intensive.

---

## Grade Distribution

| Component | Weight | Detail |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| Quizzes (3) | **30%** | 10% each &middot; Fridays of weeks 1, 2, 3 |
| Final Exam | **25%** | Cumulative &middot; Friday, July 31 |
| Participation & Engagement | **20%** | 5% per week |
| In-Class Writing Activities | **15%** | 3 per week (M / T / Th) &middot; credit / no-credit |
| Article Presentation & Discussion | **10%** | Once per student &middot; sign up Day 1 |
| **Total** | **100%** | |

---

::: {.assignment-card}
### {{< fa clipboard-check >}} Quizzes (30%)

Three quizzes given at the **end of class** on Fridays of weeks 1, 2, and 3.

::: {.assignment-meta}
**Format:** Multiple choice and short answer &middot; ~30 minutes &middot; in class
**Coverage:** That week's chapters and assigned articles
:::

[Quiz details and study guide](quizzes.qmd)
:::

---

::: {.assignment-card}
### {{< fa scroll >}} Final Exam (25%)

A cumulative exam covering all chapters, articles, and major class discussions.

::: {.assignment-meta}
**Date:** Friday, July 31, in class
**Format:** Multiple choice, short answer, applied policy question
:::

[Final exam details and study guide](final-exam.qmd)
:::

---

::: {.assignment-card}
### {{< fa pen-to-square >}} In-Class Writing Activities (15%)

A short in-class writing activity on **Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday**. Timing within the class session varies.

::: {.assignment-meta}
**Format:** ~10 minutes during class &middot; tied to that day's material
**Grading:** Credit / no-credit (√+, √, √–) &middot; cannot be made up
:::

[Writing activity details](writing-prompts.qmd)
:::

---

::: {.assignment-card}
### {{< fa person-chalkboard >}} Article Presentation & Discussion (10%)

Each student signs up on Day 1 to present and lead discussion on **one** scholarly article over the course of the term.

::: {.assignment-meta}
**Format:** 15–20 minutes total &middot; summary + discussion facilitation
**Sign-up:** Day 1 (Monday, July 6)
:::

[Article presentation guide](article-presentation.qmd)
:::

---

::: {.assignment-card}
### {{< fa comments >}} Participation & Engagement (20%)

Active engagement is essential in an intensive online format. Participation is evaluated weekly based on:

- Attending class sessions prepared to discuss the assigned readings
- Contributing thoughtful comments and questions during lecture and discussion
- Engaging substantively with peers' article presentations
- Participating in small-group exercises and chat-based activities

Given the compressed format, missing even one class represents significant lost participation. More than one unexcused absence will negatively impact your participation grade.
:::

---

::: {.info-box}
### {{< fa circle-info >}} What about take-home papers?

This course does **not** use reflection papers, policy memos, or other take-home writing assignments. All graded writing happens in class. The pace of a four-week intensive — combined with the practical realities of generative AI — makes in-class assessment a better fit for this course's goals.
:::
